# Sleep Better on Release Day: A Modern Testing Strategy for JavaScript SDKs and Components

- URL: https://ondrej.chrastina.dev/talks/sleep-better-on-release-day/
- Published: 2026-05-07
- Section: Talks
- Slides: https://ondrej.chrastina.dev/slides/Sleep%20Better%20on%20Release%20Day_%20A%20Modern%20Testing%20Strategy%20for%20JavaScript%20SDKs%20and%20Components.pdf
- Recording: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8YTQ5CciGZk

Presented at DEVWorld Amsterdam 2026 to 5,000 combined attendees. A practical guide to validating complex JavaScript SDK ecosystems - covering the Integration Matrix, the Timeline Strategy for catching browser-engine regressions weeks early, and AI Models Interoperability for non-deterministic AI features.

## What the talk was about

At the beginning of my career, Thursdays were defined by a single painful ritual: manually clicking through every button in a DXP to catch regressions. Over time that got automated. Later, managing dozens of SDKs and starters at Kontent.ai taught me how to keep a distributed ecosystem consistent.

CKEditor is a whole new level of complexity. Providing an open-source core alongside premium plugins means validating a massive plugin-based architecture where open modules interact with commercial ones - across customer environments, browser versions, and types. This talk ignored the standard Testing Pyramid and went straight to the three strategies that actually work at this scale.

## The three pillars

-   **The Integration Matrix** - testing across frameworks (React, Vue, Angular, Next.js), bundlers (Vite, webpack), and browser engines. Running sanity checks broad, deep tests targeted.
-   **The Timeline Strategy** - using canary browser lanes to catch upstream engine regressions weeks before they reach stable. A Chrome spec change was caught 3 weeks early via a PR on a nightly build lane.
-   **AI Models Interoperability** - automating tests for generative AI features where "exact match" assertions are impossible. Mocking for determinism, precision prompts to eliminate flakiness, and LLM-as-judge for semantic evaluation.

## The venue

DEVWorld Amsterdam 2026 - one of the bigger stages I've been on. 5,000 attendees on-site and online combined. The whole talk was built on real CKEditor work, with six teammates who shared their domain knowledge and real use-cases to make the examples genuine.

## Resources

-   [CKEditor QA E2E tests repo](https://github.com/ckeditor/qa-e2e-tests)
-   [Chrome canary catch example - PR #19316](https://github.com/ckeditor/ckeditor5/pull/19316)
-   [Slide deck](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1Y4qbdh1Eo3_kQZlyn-EGvzIRo5wcKLFlGparu63Qn6s/edit)

# Extreme TypeScript: Mastering Recursion and Inference via Type-Level Arithmetic

- URL: https://ondrej.chrastina.dev/talks/extreme-typescript-recursion-inference-type-level-arithmetic/
- Published: 2026-04-23
- Section: Talks
- Slides: https://ondrej.chrastina.dev/slides/Notum%20Meetup_%20Extreme%20TypeScript_%20Mastering%20Recursion%20and%20Inference%20via%20Type-Level%20Arithmetic.pdf

Meetup talk in Brno for Next.js & Strapi developers - a deep-dive into TypeScript's type system as a programming language of its own. Built around the story of a Haskell-inspired calculator with zero runtime code, teaching recursion, conditional types, and infer as practical tools for reading real library types.

## The origin story

An engineer on my team who was heavily invested in Haskell once brought something unusual to a 1-on-1: a functional calculator built entirely within TypeScript's type system - zero runtime code allowed. While practically "useless" for business logic, it turned out to be the ultimate educational tool for understanding how libraries like Zod, Prisma, and tRPC work under the hood.

## What the talk covered

-   **Counting with Tuples** - TypeScript doesn't do math natively; using `length` on Tuple types to represent numbers.
-   **Recursive Conditional Types** - how to loop without `for` loops, using recursive types for compile-time computation.
-   **Pattern Matching with `infer`** - destructuring types to extract values; the key to reading complex library definitions.
-   **Practical payoff** - de-obfuscating scary type definitions from popular libraries and debugging "Type instantiation is excessively deep" errors.

## Who it was for

Developers who use TypeScript day-to-day but find themselves copy-pasting generics from Stack Overflow without understanding them. After this talk, the mental model for recursive types and inference is concrete - not just theoretical.

## Resources

-   [Companion repository: the compile-time calculator, step by step](https://github.com/Simply007/ts-type-arithmetic)
-   [Slide deck](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/19z9qyot_uQDu-YIxbXRu0FGV9P8DQi6jkMxwfFWCwRs/edit?usp=sharing)

# CKEditor AI on Your Premises: Hook your LLM and register MCP tools

- URL: https://ondrej.chrastina.dev/talks/ckeditor-ai-on-your-premises-hook-your-llm-and-register-mcp-tools/
- Published: 2026-04-09
- Section: Talks
- Recording: https://app.zuddl.com/p/a/event/e097fef4-d67e-4606-a77d-6a16b7ab6183?utm_campaign=ckeditor_ai_onprem_webinar&utm_source=webinars_page&utm_medium=referral

A practical look at running CKEditor AI on your own infrastructure — wiring the editor to a self-hosted LLM and registering MCP tools so it can act on your data without ever leaving your premises.

## What the session covered

If you've ever shipped an enterprise feature only to hit a wall labelled "data residency," you know the pain. Your users want a co-writer that lives in the editor — your security team wants the model to live next to the database. This session walked through how to give them both.

## The moving parts

-   Hooking CKEditor AI to your own LLM endpoint — local, self-hosted, or behind your VPC.
-   Registering MCP tools so the editor can pull live context (search, lookup, retrieval) without leaking content to a third-party model.
-   Prompt routing, tool registration, and where authentication slots in.

## Who it was for

Engineering leads, AI architects, and platform teams who need rich-text AI features but can't ship anything that talks to a public model. There's always one constraint that breaks the obvious approach — on-premises is usually it.

# Case Study: Enterprise AI Content Creation Gaps

- URL: https://ondrej.chrastina.dev/talks/enterprise-ai-content-creation-gaps-drupalcon-chicago-2026/
- Published: 2026-03-25
- Section: Talks
- Recording: https://events.drupal.org/chicago2026

DrupalCon Chicago 2026 session unpacking the real "AI gaps" enterprises hit in content workflows - the urgency trap, trust and compliance hurdles, the breadth-vs-depth problem, and why calling a model API is the easy part. Presents CKEditor AI as the embedded solution.

## What the session covered

The "Bring Your Own AI" era has arrived - but for agencies and their enterprise clients, it often creates disconnected workflows and new headaches instead of productivity gains. This session shared patterns from dozens of enterprise discovery calls, revealing the real gaps teams hit when they try to put generative AI into their content pipelines.

## The four enterprise AI gaps

-   **Urgency vs. strategy** - the pressure to "do AI now" clashes with starting with real, well-scoped workflows. The teams that ship something durable start small and focused.
-   **Trust** - security, compliance, and data governance still gate adoption. Moderation, telemetry, and logging aren't optional at enterprise scale.
-   **Breadth vs. depth** - a ChatGPT licence isn't a content strategy. The model is only as useful as the context and domain knowledge you give it.
-   **API vs. flows** - calling a model is easy. User value is hard. Context, permissions, and workflow integration are where the real work is.

## The solution frame

The session introduced CKEditor AI as the embedded enterprise solution that addresses all four gaps: AI Chat, AI Review, and AI Quick Actions working directly inside the authoring workspace - with the security, compliance, and governance controls enterprise teams require.

## The venue

DrupalCon Chicago 2026 - a 4-day event celebrating 25 years of Drupal, with an AI-sponsored summit on day one. The whole conference was framed around AI readiness in the Drupal ecosystem.

# Extreme TypeScript: Mastering Recursion and Inference via Type-Level Arithmetic

- URL: https://ondrej.chrastina.dev/talks/extreme-typescript-mastering-recursion-and-inference-via-type-level-arithmetic/
- Published: 2026-01-13
- Section: Talks
- Slides: https://github.com/Simply007/ts-type-arithmetic/blob/cdb7cfaec98c973494b24915148931a267b74f13/assets/Extreme%20TypeScript_%20Mastering%20Recursion%20and%20Inference%20via%20Type-Level%20Arithmetic.pdf

Deep dive into advanced TypeScript type system features by building a compile-time calculator. Master conditional types, the infer keyword, template literal types, tuple manipulation, and recursive type definitions through practical, step-by-step examples. Learn to write type-level programs that perform arithmetic at compile time.

A few years ago, an engineer on my team who was heavily invested in Haskell and declarative programming brought something unusual to our 1-on-1. It was a functional calculator built entirely within TypeScript's type system—zero runtime code allowed. 

While practically "useless" for business logic, I realized it was the ultimate educational tool for demonstrating the raw power of the language. In this talk, we will deconstruct that experiment. We won't just look at code; we will learn how to **read and write** the complex constructs that power libraries like Zod, Prisma, or tRPC. You will learn how to manipulate **Tuples for counting**, master **Recursive Conditional Types**, and use `**infer**` to unwrap data. By the end, you won't just know how to add numbers in types—you will possess the mental framework to debug the most terrifying generic errors your library throws at you.

# AI Master Podcast: Building the Future of Content Editing with Al

- URL: https://ondrej.chrastina.dev/talks/ai-master-podcast-building-the-future-of-content-editing-with-al/
- Published: 2025-12-14
- Section: Talks
- Recording: https://creators.spotify.com/pod/profile/ai-master/episodes/AIMP-07-Ondej-Chrastina-Building-the-Future-of-Content-Editing-with-AI-e3ccqr1

AI Master Podcast episode with Ondřej Chrastina (Developer Advocate at CKEditor) on AI-powered content editing. Learn how CKEditor 5 differs from CKEditor 4 (model-based architecture vs DOM), why it’s easier to extend with plugins, and how it supports collaboration, versioning, and track changes. We discuss CKEditor AI features for content ideation, drafting, rewriting, and review while preserving formatting, user control, safety, privacy, and GDPR. Practical insights on integrating LLMs into rich text editors, handling latency and hallucinations, prompt vs context engineering, multilingual challenges, and measuring AI productivity.

This episode is also available on YouTube:

[Future of Content Editing with AI](https://youtu.be/DVQilLE2PRE)

In this episode of the AI Master Podcast, I’m joined by Ondřej Chrastina, Developer Advocate at CKEditor and an experienced Developer Relations leader with over 12 years of hands-on and leadership experience in building outstanding developer experience for complex platforms.

Ondřej shares his professional journey — from QA engineering and software development, through building internal tooling and SDKs, to establishing and leading Developer Relations programs at companies such as Kentico, Kontent.ai, Ataccama, and now CKEditor. We talk about how deep empathy for developer pain points shapes better products, tooling, and documentation.

A large part of our conversation focuses on CKEditor 5 — its modern, extensible architecture and the challenges of using rich-text editors in today’s web applications. We explore how generative AI and large language models can meaningfully enhance content editing, turning editors into intelligent assistants rather than passive tools.

Ondřej explains practical AI use cases such as content suggestions, summarization, auto-formatting, review workflows, and AI-assisted collaboration. We also go deep into the technical and product challenges of embedding AI into editors: latency, context management, hallucinations, prompt engineering, safety, and maintaining full user control — especially in enterprise environments where privacy, data governance, and GDPR compliance are critical.

We also discuss the future of rich-text editors in an AI-driven world, the role of open source and community contributions, multilingual challenges, and which AI advancements (embeddings, RAG, multimodal models) are most exciting for the next generation of editor experiences.

To wrap up, we switch to a more personal perspective — continuous learning, staying motivated as a software engineer, productivity, travel, and a few lesser-known facts about Ondřej.

## Key topics covered in this episode:

-   Architecting AI-powered features in rich-text editors while preserving user control
-   Integrating LLMs into editors: latency, context size, and hallucination challenges
-   Prompt engineering patterns for editor-based AI workflows
-   Privacy, GDPR, and data governance in enterprise-grade AI integrations
-   The future of rich-text editors as intelligent, collaborative assistants

# Empowering the TYPO3 Community: Introducing CKEditor Pack for Enhanced Content Creation

- URL: https://ondrej.chrastina.dev/talks/empowering-the-typo3-community-introducing-ckeditor-pack-for-enhanced-content-creation/
- Published: 2025-11-25
- Section: Talks
- Slides: https://ondrej.chrastina.dev/slides/CKEditor%20Pack%20for%20Enhanced%20Content%20Creation.pdf

Open-Source, Open-Future: Our Vision for TYPO3 and CKEditor introduces the CKEditor Pack, a community-driven initiative designed to modernize content editing in TYPO3. The talk explores how open-source collaboration, a unified plugin ecosystem, and thoughtful editor experience design come together to simplify configuration while unlocking advanced editing capabilities.

At **T3CON TYPO3 Conference**, this talk presented the **CKEditor Pack** as a new open-source initiative created to enhance and unify rich content editing in TYPO3. Built specifically for the TYPO3 ecosystem, the CKEditor Pack brings together a curated set of editing, collaboration, and productivity features while preserving the familiar TYPO3 look and feel. The goal is simple: reduce fragmentation, simplify configuration, and make advanced editing capabilities accessible out of the box.

[CKEditor pack for TYPO3](https://extensions.typo3.org/extension/rte_ckeditor_pack)

The session walks through the motivation behind the project, inspired by successful community models in other CMS ecosystems, and highlights how existing free plugins and maintainers can contribute to a shared, sustainable solution. Through practical examples and a live-style demonstration, the talk shows the benefits for different roles. Editors gain faster, cleaner workflows; admins get better governance and consistency. Integrators benefit from modular architecture and extensibility; and contributors are invited to actively shape the future of the project.

As an open-source, community-first effort, the CKEditor Pack represents a long-term vision for TYPO3 editing: collaborative, powerful, and built together with the ecosystem. The session concludes with a look ahead at what’s next and how the TYPO3 community can get involved.  
🔗 Presented at: [https://t3con.typo3.com/](https://t3con.typo3.com/)

## Abstract

Join me to explore a new community initiative by **T3Planet** and **CKEditor** aimed at transforming content editing in TYPO3. In this session, I will demonstrate the open-source **CKEditor Pack**, showcasing how it solves everyday challenges through advanced features like real-time collaboration, improved formatting workflows, and seamless media handling all within the familiar TYPO3 environment. This session is not just a demo, but an invitation: be part of the conversation and discover how you can help shape the future of this project to meet the real needs of the TYPO3 community.

## What the session covered

Have you ever uploaded a 12 MB hero image into a CMS field that absolutely did not need 12 MB? I have. Image handling is one of those quiet bottlenecks — too easy to ignore, too painful to keep ignoring. Slow uploads, oversize assets, unnecessary processing on the client, formats that don't play nicely on mobile. The cumulative cost is real.

## The deep dive

-   What the CKEditor Image Optimizer (powered by Uploadcare) actually does — under the hood.
-   Configuration and plug-in steps: where it slots into an existing CKEditor setup.
-   Trade-offs and gotchas — there's always one.
-   What changes for authors and what changes on the CDN bill.

## Who it was for

Developers handling rich media in CKEditor, content engineers who own the upload pipeline, and anyone tired of asking authors to please just compress the JPEG. Voila — a workflow that does it for them.

# Add Template & Mention Plugins to Existing Project

- URL: https://ondrej.chrastina.dev/talks/add-template-and-mention-plugins-to-existing-project/
- Published: 2025-09-23
- Section: Talks
- Recording: https://youtu.be/ZiW2Mu04gR0

Part of the MLH 2025 series. I walked through two paths for adding Template and Mention plugins to an existing CKEditor 5 project — the fast route via CKEditor builder, and the manual integration when the scenario gets messy.

## What this MLH 2025 session was about

I bet most of you have shipped a CKEditor integration and then been asked to add "just one more plugin" a quarter later. Templates? @mentions? Both? Suddenly you're staring at a webpack config wondering if you should rebuild from scratch. You don't have to.

## Two paths I walked through

-   **CKEditor builder** — assemble a new build with the extra plugins. Fast path, copy-paste ready.
-   **Manual integration** — for projects that have outgrown the builder UI: importing the plugin packages, wiring the toolbar, and registering the configuration.
-   **Iteration discipline** — clean development cycles that don't break what's already in production.

## Who it was for

Developers with a working CKEditor 5 integration who need to extend it, particularly with Templates and Mention plugins. Practical, focused, no fluff — that was the whole point of the MLH 2025 series. All right, we're done!

# From Vanilla JS starter to TypeScript GitHub repo

- URL: https://ondrej.chrastina.dev/talks/from-vanilla-js-starter-to-typescript-github-repo/
- Published: 2025-09-23
- Section: Talks
- Recording: https://youtu.be/5lGozI_-Ds8

Part of the MLH 2025 series. I took a CKEditor 5 vanilla JavaScript starter all the way to a real TypeScript GitHub repo — types, tooling, and a build setup another developer can clone and run.

## What this MLH 2025 session was about

Having written a good share of JavaScript code, I wanted to expand a CKEditor 5 starter into something I'd actually merge into production. That meant moving off the vanilla JS demo and into a TypeScript GitHub repo with types, lint, and a clean build pipeline.

## The journey

-   Starting point — the CKEditor 5 vanilla JS starter.
-   Migrating to TypeScript — tsconfig, type imports for CKEditor 5 packages, and the small gotchas in between.
-   Setting up the GitHub repo — scripts, CI-friendly structure, and a setup another developer can clone and run.
-   Where the type definitions actually pay off (and where they're just compile-time noise).

## Who it was for

Developers comfortable with JS but new to TypeScript, especially those starting from the CKEditor 5 starter and ready to graduate to a real repo. Yippee — what a fun one to put together.

# Spark Team Productivity with a Frictionless, Unified AI Writing Stack

- URL: https://ondrej.chrastina.dev/talks/spark-team-productivity-with-a-frictionless-unified-ai-writing-stack/
- Published: 2025-09-15
- Section: Talks
- Slides: https://ondrej.chrastina.dev/slides/Spark%20Team%20Productivity%20with%20a%20Frictionless,%20Unified%20AI%20Writing%20Stack.pdf
- Recording: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N5DDRzJtBTY&list=PLKzl1AGxt2J3CtQzdUdNRBHS4lw-LIalL&index=1

The talk introduces CKEditor AI, a groundbreaking add-on that seamlessly integrates AI capabilities into CKEditor. This innovation enables the AI to think and generate content in rich text format while preserving complex formatting. Designed for direct integration into your application, CKEditor AI offers a unified, secure, and flecible platform for content creation and editing.

In this lightning talk delivered at The AI Conference 2025, I address the growing friction and security risks caused by the "Bring Your Own AI" (BYOAI) trend, where 78% of workers use external AI tools to generate content. I highlight how copying and pasting from external chatbots breaks formatting (tables, lists) and introduces compliance vulnerabilities for enterprises.

**CKEditor AI** is designed to solve these, a new suite of capabilities integrated directly into the rich text editor. Unlike external tools, CKEditor AI is aware of the document model, meaning it preserves complex formatting during generation and editing. The talk outlines three core components of the solution:

-   **AI Chat:** A context-aware assistant capable of drafting content (e.g., support ticket replies) directly in the editor.
-   **Quick Actions:** Pre-configured commands for repetitive tasks like translation, summarization, or tone adjustment.
-   **AI Content Review:** A specialized interface similar to "track changes" designed to handle high volumes of AI suggestions, ideal for regulatory audits or grammar checks.

The talk is concluded by emphasizing that the solution creates a unified, secure environment for content creation that eliminates the chaos of external tools while maintaining enterprise-grade compliance.

## Abstract:

Your content creators, marketers, and support teams are juggling tools. They draft and experiment with content in multiple conversational AI systems. The result is a tedious copy-paste job into your application or internal system, followed by hours spent fixing the formatting that inevitably breaks. For them, it's inefficient. But for you - the founders, the product leaders, the developers - it is a nightmare. This 'Bring Your Own AI' chaos creates security holes, opens you up to compliance risks, and produces content that is inconsistent and often factually incorrect because it lacks critical context. The workflow is fundamentally broken.

Let’s explore the challenges and opportunities of integrating AI directly into your content creation process. We will touch on how integrating AI into your writing stack can help you:

-   Boost productivity and alignment
    -   Give your users a unified platform with tailored AI
    -   Preserve rich text formatting 
    -   Get an AI-driven editing experience and review process without friction
-   Offload the operational burden
    -   Reduce the workload on AIOps teams
-   Keep your product or application compliant and secure

CKEditor has been the most trusted, robust rich text editor component on the market for over two decades - built for engineers and trusted by Fortune 500 companies. In this talk, we’ll unveil the new CKEditor AI: a suite of configurable components thaxt brings context‑aware generation, predefined quick actions, model selection, and review workflows directly into your rich text editor. Alongside integrated real-time collaboration, you get elevated rich text editing, a productivity boost, and a coherent user experience all in one place.

Based on research with our customers, we will showcase possible applications of an integrated AI writing stack such as audit reports, translation workflows, or customer service sentiment analysis.

Join us for this talk to learn more about what you can achieve with the unified AI writing stack

  

**Read the full recap of CKEditor's experience at the conference here:**

[AI Conference 2025 - CKEditor in da house](https://dev.to/ckeditor/ai-conference-2025-ckeditor-in-da-house-m11)

# Building a blazing fast application with Gatsby.js

- URL: https://ondrej.chrastina.dev/talks/building-a-blazing-fast-application-with-gatsby-js/
- Published: 2019-09-15
- Section: Talks

Overview how Gtabsy source plugin is building the websites, it's speed benefits. And how JamStack in combination with headless CMS can help you to build blazing fast, secure and highly available site. Esp in combination withe Kentico Cloud (now Kontent.ai) headless CMS. Presented on Kentico Connection (Brno) 2019.

The Gatsby source plugin plays a crucial role in building websites by enabling seamless integration between Gatsby.js and various data sources, such as headless CMS platforms. This plugin efficiently fetches data during the build process, allowing developers to pre-render static pages that are highly optimized for speed. By leveraging this approach, websites can deliver exceptional performance, as the static content is served directly from a Content Delivery Network (CDN), reducing load times significantly.

The combination of JamStack architecture and a headless CMS further enhances the capabilities of modern web development. JamStack focuses on pre-rendering and decoupling the frontend from the backend, which not only improves speed but also enhances security by minimizing server-side vulnerabilities. A headless CMS, such as Kontent.ai, acts as a content repository that provides structured data via APIs. This enables developers to build blazing fast, secure, and highly available websites that are easy to scale and maintain.

For more information about the Gtabs ysource plugin and how it connects Gatsby.js with headless CMS solutions, visit the official GitHub repository: [https://github.com/kontent-ai/gatsby-packages](https://github.com/kontent-ai/gatsby-packages).
